pr_title: STM32 devices support AHB prescaler value in range 1-512
pr_body:
The DTS can accept a ahb-prescaler  >1 and <512 to reduce the SYSCLOCK to the HCLK.


FIxes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/37173

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu <francois.ramu@st.com>
pr_comments:
rebase
align the possible values with the `drivers/clock_control/Kconfig.stm32`

- stm32wb and stm32wl   exclude the `<ahb-prescaler> `  property from the st,stm32-rcc.yaml and define their own ahb1-prescaler

- stm32H7 does not include the st,stm32-rcc.yaml and define its own `<hpre>` property

updating the description in the yaml files
and rebase

remove STM32_AHB_PRESCALER > 1 for stm32U5
and rebase

issue_context.title: drivers: clock_control: stm32: AHB prescaler usable for almost all stm32 series
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
As highlighted in #37139 review, most of STM32 have Systick and Core clock on the same HCLK clock.
The following comments, which could be found in **clock_stm32_ll_common.c** (but not only),
is wrong. 
It is possible to have STM32_AHB_PRESCALER != 1, but we need to take to compute HCLK as base in zephyr (and don't use SYSCLK which is not core clock).
Note: there may be some exception, and a special attention is required for dualcore series.
```
#if STM32_AHB_PRESCALER > 1
/*
 * AHB prescaler allows to set a HCLK frequency (feeding cortex systick)
 * lower than SYSCLK frequency (actual core frequency).
 * Though, zephyr doesn't make a difference today between these two clocks.
 * So, changing this prescaler is not allowed until it is made possible to
 * use them independently in zephyr clock subsystem.
 */
#error "AHB prescaler can't be higher than 1"
#endif 
```

review_comments: The same comment is present in stm32U5 specific file and should be removed
